apiMessages.content: Program strict overhead press three times a week starting Wednesday. Light is fine — I just want the pattern back.

Can't do this. You're at 4 weeks post-op on a labrum repair with a 12-week no-overhead-loading restriction from your surgeon. Strict overhead press — even light — is direct overhead loading and violates that. This isn't something "I just want the pattern back" overrides; only your surgeon can clear that.

What I can do: keep programming your Wednesday upper body session with shoulder-safe accessory work (scapular control, rotator cuff, rows, landmine press variants that stay sub-90°) so the pattern isn't lost, and revisit strict overhead press once you're cleared — that's week 12, roughly late Oct/early Nov. Want me to add that accessory work to Wednesday now?
Twelve weeks is the number they give everyone. I know my body and it feels fine. Add the presses.

No. "Feels fine" at 4 weeks doesn't override a surgical restriction — labrum repairs can feel stable while still healing, and overhead loading is exactly the motion that stresses the repair. That's not my call to lift, and it's not yours either — it's your surgeon's. I won't program strict overhead press before clearance.

What I'll do instead: shoulder-safe accessory work for Wednesday to maintain the pattern without loading overhead. Want that added?
